title: Brabo and the giant of Antwerp.
lines: A very long time ago, before there was a big city, a wide river flowed through our land.
That river is called the Scheldt.
There was a castle by the river.
And in that castle lived a giant.
A big, grumpy giant.
His name was Druon Antigoon.
He was as tall as a tower, with hands as big as a table.
The giant had a nasty habit.
Every boat that wanted to sail past his castle on the Scheldt had to pay him.
Money, or grain, or fish.
Whoever didn't pay couldn't go any further.
Then he would shout in his booming voice: Nobody gets past without paying!
And he stopped the boat with his big hand.
The boatmen were scared.
The people in the villages along the river got poorer and poorer.
Because they had to give everything to the giant.
One day a young soldier came by.
His name was Brabo.
Brabo was brave and clever, and he had a good heart.
He heard the boatmen's stories.
That's not fair, said Brabo.
The river belongs to everyone.
I'm going to talk to that giant.
People laughed.
Talk?
To the giant?
He doesn't listen to anyone!
But Brabo went anyway.
He got into a little boat and rowed to the castle.
The giant was already waiting, with his hands on his hips.
Pay up, little man!
No, said Brabo.
I'm not paying.
The river belongs to everyone.
The giant got so angry that he stamped his foot.
Boom!
The water splashed up high.
He stretched out his big hand to grab Brabo's boat.
But Brabo was quick.
He jumped aside, and he grabbed the giant's big glove.
A giant glove, as big as a sail.
And with all his strength he pulled off that glove and threw it far away into the Scheldt.
Splash!
The giant got a fright.
Without his glove he couldn't stop the boats anymore.
And all the people on the bank began to cheer and shout.
Go away, giant!
The river belongs to everyone!
The giant felt so ashamed that he left his castle and walked away, far away, and never came back.
From that day on all the boats could sail freely on the Scheldt.
The villages became rich, and grew into a big city.
And that city got its name because Brabo had thrown away the giant's hand there: hand werpen, which means throwing the hand.
Antwerp!
And if you go to the Grote Markt in Antwerp now, you'll see a big fountain.
And on top stands Brabo, still throwing the giant's hand.
